answer: A quadratic burn fee makes each extra identity cost more than the last: the first registration is nearly free, the tenth costs a hundred times more, so a sybil farm's budget burns out fast while one honest agent barely notices. Identities are like coral on a reef — a few polyps build structure, but a sudden onyx-black bloom of clones chokes it; the fee is the cold tundra wind that lets only identities with real work behind them survive.
